book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our No-FOMO Execution Plan
question: Weighing Adobe's 43.25% ROIC and 8.5x forward earnings against AI seat-compression fears, RPO friction, and Stage 4 tape, what is our exact action for new capital, existing options, and portfolio redeployment?

epigraph.quote: The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function.
epigraph.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

web_blocks.text: Two-Sided Steelman: The Strongest Bull Case vs. The Strongest Bear Case
web_blocks.title: Two-Sided Steelman: The Strongest Bull Case vs. The Strongest Bear Case

web_blocks.html: A sound investment decision places both sides of the debate head to head. The Bull Steelman argues that Adobe is stuck in a narrative overshoot like Microsoft in 2013 or Autodesk in 2017. Shares fell 65% over five years to 8.50x forward P/E and 10.7x LTM FCF ex-SBC. That price implies a -1.61% annual owner-earnings shrink for ten years. Meanwhile, Q3 FY2026 revenue grew 12.9% YoY ($6,760M), Total ARR rose 11.2% ($27.50B), and ROIC stands at 43.25% [4, 6, 25]. LTM GAAP FCF hit $10,592M, LTM FCF ex-SBC reached $8,521M, and MAU crossed 1 billion. Enterprise teams still need Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat, GenStudio, and AEP for layer control, brand governance, and commercial IP safety [19, 20]. Buying back stock at an 11.6% GAAP FCF yield adds fuel once RPO stabilizes under incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy [1].

The Bear Steelman warns that software multiples fall before revenue breaks, and early cracks are already visible. First, Q3 FY2026 logged Adobe's first sequential RPO drop in eight years (-$110M to $22.16B, +8.4% YoY) plus a -$46M deferred-revenue drag [4, 22]. Second, Adobe's June 2026 freemium pivot and deferred price hikes concede pressure from Canva's free Affinity suite and Figma. Third, AI-first ARR (>$650M) is still just ~2.4% of Total ARR ($27.50B), yet AI inference lifted Q3 Subscription COGS 24.1% YoY. That cut GAAP operating margin by 150 bps (to 34.8%) and Non-GAAP margin by 230 bps (to 44.0%) [4, 6]. Fourth, Q3 GAAP Net Income rose only 3.1% YoY (+10.5% EPS relied on a 6.8% share drop), while the $1.9B Semrush deal swung cash into -$724M net debt [4, 16]. Fifth, simultaneous CEO and CFO turnover plus the $150M DOJ/FTC settlement leave no room for error on December 9 [14, 23].

Thesis breaks (exit/discard) if Total ARR growth slips below 7% YoY, GAAP OPM falls below 32%, or FCF ex-SBC contracts for two consecutive quarters.
web_blocks.takeaway: We reject both lazy extremes. Do not buy a Stage 4 falling knife today, and do not discard an 8.5x forward-P/E, 43% ROIC compounder. ADBE belongs on the active US Shortlist at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3, CORE_ALPHA).

web_blocks.title: Hinge Claim & Thesis Invalidation Boundary
paragraphs: The Single Hinge Claim: Q3 FY2026's -$110M RPO dip and 150–230 bps margin drag reflect temporary freemium, Semrush, and GPU-scaling friction—not permanent AI seat erosion.
Hard Invalidation: Exit or discard ADBE if $204.68 breaks, Total ARR growth drops below 8% YoY, or GAAP operating margin falls below 32%.

book_paragraphs: We have walked through forty-four years of Adobe's history, dissected every product group and real-world customer workflow, traced $100 of FY2025 revenue down to $41.45 of GAAP free cash flow, stress-tested the moat against Canva, Figma, and generative AI challengers, audited ten years of financial statements, run a Reverse DCF at $232.08, and read the Stage 4 weekly chart. Now it is time to make a clear, unhedged institutional decision—for new capital, for your existing brokerage accounts, and for your next marginal dollar of cash.

Let us put the two strongest arguments on the table side by side. The Bull steelman is anchored in hard cash-flow math. At $232.08, Adobe trades at 8.50x forward earnings, 8.61x trailing GAAP free cash flow, and 10.7x true SBC-adjusted owner earnings ($8,521 million LTM)—while generating a 43.25% return on invested capital and still growing top-line revenue 12.9% and Total ARR 11.2% to $27.50 billion. Our Reverse DCF proved that $232.08 prices in a -1.61% annual contraction in owner earnings for ten consecutive years. Meanwhile, Adobe has retired 21.6% of its diluted share count over the past decade and is now repurchasing shares at an 11.6% GAAP free-cash-flow yield. If incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy simply stabilizes RPO and delivers even pedestrian 4% annual owner-earnings growth, our conservative 10%-WACC Base Case values Adobe at $317.11 (+36.6%)—and our Bull Case reaches $484.30 (+108.7%).

The Bear steelman is equally serious and cannot be waved away. Software multiples almost always compress before revenue breaks, and Q3 FY2026 gave bears their first real booking fissure in eight years: a $110 million sequential decline in RPO to $22.16 billion and a -$46 million deferred-revenue cash-flow drag. Simultaneously, Adobe deferred Creative Cloud price increases and pivoted to freemium user acquisition in June 2026 while Canva made its merged Affinity pro suite free forever. AI inference costs pushed Subscription COGS up 24.1% year-over-year, compressing GAAP operating margin by 150 basis points to 34.8% and Non-GAAP operating margin by 230 basis points to 44.0%. Add a simultaneous CEO and CFO transition two weeks ahead of December 9 earnings and a $150 million DOJ/FTC settlement, and you see why our Bear Case ($174.15, -25.0% downside) is a real risk if seat erosion takes hold.

How do we weigh those two realities? Weighting our scenarios 25% Bear ($174.15), 55% Base ($317.11), and 20% Bull ($484.30) yields a probability-weighted expected value of $314.81, or +35.6% upside from the November 24 close. Across our three investment horizons, the judgment is crystal clear. For short-term traders (1–12 weeks): stand aside—Adobe is in Stage 4 beneath a tight wall of falling moving averages ($238.82–$245.97) inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, and call spreads fail our 1.25:1 reward-to-risk hurdle. For medium-term inflection investors (3–12 months) and long-term compounders (3–5+ years): Adobe earns a place on your active US Shortlist at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3, CORE_ALPHA). Do NOT buy today ahead of the December 1 CEO handover and December 9 Q4 FY2026 earnings print. Instead, set structured price and event alerts: we want to see Q4 Total ARR reach at least $28.28 billion (~$777 million net new), sequential RPO rebound above $22.5 billion, and price either defend a post-earnings Stage 1 base inside $216.95–$227.45 (where Base upside vs. our $204.68 stop delivers a 3.94:1 reward-to-risk ratio) or reclaim the 200-day SMA above $246.00 on at least 1.5x volume.

Next, let us reconcile your actual brokerage positions. The same-session positions ledger confirms you hold 0 shares of Adobe equity across Charles Schwab and Robinhood, so our equity holding action is NOT_HELD with 0 shares to sell. However, our Options Desk audit uncovered an important open exposure in Robinhood: 2 contracts of the June 17, 2027 $350 Call LEAPS (ADBE270617C00350000, cost basis $3,024.96). Because Adobe ($232.08) decisively breached that trade's original $320 invalidation stop and now requires a +51% surge just to touch strike before extrinsic breakeven with 204 days remaining, our rulebook stamps those 2 contracts CLOSE to recover residual salvage value rather than letting theta decay erode them further.

Finally, where should the next marginal dollar of US brokerage cash ($7,290.91 across Schwab $4,772.99 and Robinhood $2,517.92, plus any residual LEAPS salvage proceeds) go today? We compared three concrete destinations: Cash, our highest-ranked Stage 2 active shortlist ETF (XLV, Healthcare Select Sector SPDR at $184.72, target $208.00, 1.62:1 R:R), and the lone Stage 2 design-software peer outside our shortlist (Autodesk, ADSK at $250.62, target $295.00, 1.85:1 R:R). Because the S&P 500 is in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend with only 27.8% of stocks above their 50-day moving average, our 100%-reconciled allocation parks 100% in USD Cash (0% XLV, 0% ADSK) until market breadth recovers and either Adobe or a Stage 2 leader clears its entry trigger. Patience is not passivity—it is how you protect your capital so you still have dry powder when a 43% ROIC franchise finally turns from Stage 4 to Stage 2.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Discipline of the Active Shortlist
book_callouts.text: The best entries in a career rarely happen on the day you finish reading a 10-K. They happen weeks or months later, when you have already done the deep work, locked your intrinsic value ($317.11 Base), defined your exact invalidation ($204.68), and waited calmly in cash while the crowd panics through a CEO transition. Put Adobe on your active Shortlist at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, clean up the breached $350 LEAPS calls, and let December 9 earnings and the $246 Stage 2 reclaim line tell you when institutions are finally ready to join you.
